title: Usage versus results: routes, target earning and waiver opportunity cost

materials_reviewed.note: Accessible article text was reviewed. No video viewing, paid player-profile access or independent chart/table audit is claimed.

sources.author: Matt Harmon
sources.title: Introduction to Reception Perception
sources.material_reviewed: Accessible methodology/explanatory body and retrospective examples; paid player profiles not accessed.
sources.lesson: Route, coverage and alignment evidence can help distinguish receiver performance from quarterback and box-score effects.
caveats: Reception Perception Route Percentage is the distribution of route types, not routes per team dropback.
Historical hit rates are retrospective and are not calibrated forward probabilities.

sources.author: Mike Anderson
sources.title: Targets Per Route Run Report: 2026 Season Preview (Fantasy Football)
sources.material_reviewed: Accessible explanatory body and displayed historical table; table not independently audited.
sources.lesson: TPRR means targets divided by routes. Evaluate target earning alongside route opportunity, rather than interpreting either alone.
caveats: Small samples, quarterback, scheme, role, target depth and touchdown variance complicate comparisons.
Percentage bands are heuristics, not universal validated thresholds.

sources.author: Sam Sherman
sources.title: Dominate the Waiver Wire: Top Five Tips
sources.material_reviewed: Accessible methodology, findings and tips; embedded charts not independently transcribed.
sources.lesson: Consider talent, competition, offensive environment, bench opportunity cost and changing seasonal needs when studying waiver value.
caveats: Historical analysis predates 2023 and uses five bench slots plus a kicker; league transfer requires adjustment.
Retrospective scoring weeks do not establish that a player was predictably startable.

analytical_proposals.proposal: Study changes in route participation together with target earning and role context, then compare those signals with later production. A scoring spike alone should not be treated as evidence of a durable role change.
definitions: Provider-defined routes and the denominator for route participation must be recorded.
TPRR = targets/routes; preserve the raw targets and routes as well as the rate.
Receiving skill, opportunity and realized fantasy points are different measurements.

analytical_proposals.proposal: When the existing league decision process evaluates a candidate, compare plausible future utility with the roster spot and acquisition resources consumed; examine results after accounting for whether the player was reasonably startable.

risks_and_limits: Definitions and sample windows may differ across providers. Do not merge incompatible route metrics.
Injury absences, quarterback changes, game script and schedule may confound apparent signal performance.
Research must preserve negative examples and rejected candidates to limit selection and survivorship bias.
Retrospective evidence supports questions to test; it does not establish a current player forecast or a guaranteed breakout.
No numerical edge, signal weight, universal cutoff or new governing rule has been validated by this reading.

prospective_test_plan.objective: Determine whether combined opportunity and target-earning evidence improves league-specific role-change identification beyond recent fantasy points alone.
prospective_test_plan.selection: Define the future player pool and observation window before evaluating outcomes; retain all assessed cases and reasons for inclusion.
inputs_to_capture: Routes, team dropbacks when available, targets and TPRR
Injury, quarterback, depth-chart and game-script context
Relevant league format and authenticated availability only if actionable advice is contemplated
prospective_test_plan.forecast_handling: This note creates no forecast. If the established Brain later makes a material recommendation, preserve its original contemporaneous prediction, evidence, uncertainty and deadline in the existing decision ledger.
prospective_test_plan.evaluation: After the chosen future windows finish, compare subsequent role persistence and fantasy production with a simple recent-points baseline. Grade decision process independently from results and separate actual user action from advice.
prospective_test_plan.adoption_gate: Treat findings as provisional across multiple observations. Any adopted rule belongs in the repository's existing versioned learning system, not this research note.
prospective_test_plan.aggregation: When combining games, aggregate compatible raw counts before recomputing rates. Preserve sample sizes, source definitions and explicit context exclusions.
prospective_test_plan.baselines: Compare with a highest-projected-eligible-player baseline when available, and optionally a recent-points baseline, under the same eligibility, deadline and resource constraints.
outcome_dimensions: Workload forecast error when a forecast was actually recorded
Useful starts and points above an available replacement
Actual acquisition cost when an acquisition occurred
Role error versus touchdown or yardage variance

preservation.correction_policy: Preserve this dated note; document later corrections or evidence in a new dated record referencing it.

league_context.format: Full PPR; two FLEX; seven bench; no kicker
league_context.relevance: Translate the waiver article's five-bench, kicker-containing example to this format before testing any conclusion. Current player ownership, availability and prices are not asserted here.
